items.title: Russell Brand Issues Statement, Says He Is 'Not Guilty' Amid Rape Sentence
items.summary:
Russell Brand has issued a statement from prison, claiming that he is “not guilty” after being sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault.

“Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,” the comedian, 51, said in a statement shared by his wife, Laura Brand , via his YouTube channel on Sunday, November 15.

Laura, 39, has begun by stating that “Russell has asked me to read something to you today,” before turning to a notebook to recall her husband’s message. The YouTube post served as the first time Laura had publicly addressed Russell’s conviction and prison sentence , which was delivered in London’s Southwark Crown Court on Monday, November 9.

Russell’s message continued, “The good news is that Christ is with us when we choose him, and I do. I am incarcerated in HMP Littlehey. Little as in small, and hey as in, ‘Hey, I’m in the biggest sex offenders prison in Europe.’ The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated. And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.”

Russell Brand's Dad Claims His Son Is a Victim After Sentencing 

Russell went to trial for four weeks, ultimately found guilty by a jury on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. Russell had repeatedly denied accusations of wrongdoing, and was found not guilty on two other rape charges and an attempted indecent assault charge.

Laura, who…

The story line was a departure from the usual format , which usually shows Colter on the road solving a variety of cases week to week. He will largely interact with his team over the phone, so showcasing the characters all in one place marks a shakeup for Tracker.

Tracker quickly found success when it premiered in 2024, following fictional survivalist Colter as he helped solve numerous missing persons cases. items.title: Tom Arnold, 67, Calls People His Age 'Disgusting,' Admits He Hasn't Dated
items.summary:
Tom Arnold is opening up about his dating mindset amid his ongoing hiatus from the romance scene.

“I used to say, people are like — because I haven’t had a date for nine and a half years — ‘You should date someone your own age,’” Arnold, 67, told Page Six in an interview published on Friday, November 13. “And I’m like, ‘Dude, have you seen people my age? We are freaking disgusting.’”

“But here’s the thing,” he continued, “I have learned there’s a lot of funny, smart, sexy, 60-something women. … But I’ll tell you what they’re not looking for. They’re not looking for a guy that used to have a lot of money and now has two little kids. They are like, ‘Forget that. That is not what I’m looking for.’”

Arnold, who confirmed he was serious about wanting to find love again, shared that “it would be good to love somebody and be loved.”

“I love my kids so much. There’s a lot of love there. And my buddies,” he said. “But I’ll be OK. You know, I’ve had four marriages.”

Arnold was previously married to Roseanne Barr from 1990 to 1994, Julie Armstrong from 1995 to 1999, Shelby Ross from 2002 to 2008 and Ashley Groussman from 2009 to 2020. Arnold and Groussman share two children: son Jax, 13, and daughter Quinn, 10.

In 2025, Arnold got candid about his marriage to Barr while promoting his My Crazy X-Wife comedy tour.

“People say ‘My Crazy X-Wife, oh, I know which one that is. It’s Roseanne,’” he told Us . “And I’m like, ‘She’s not even close to my craziest ex-wife because we didn’t have kids together.’ The…

Ashley shared that she and her mom “talked about this a lot,” noting that she tried to convince her mother not to discuss politics in the operating rome where they might be an “orderly with immigration status or a person of color there to facilitate in this operation and this white woman with a lot of status and a lot of fame and a lot of prestige — she makes a big impact everywhere she goes, especially on Williamson County Hospital — had the word Trump written on her inner thigh.”

“And she didn’t take that position with me,” Ashley continued. “I won’t quote what she said back to me, but we differed in that.”

“What my mom really wanted me to do was to see that from her perspective,” she explained. “And I could, but I also still think about that orderly, whoever else was there. I even tried to frame it as a title seven workplace discrimination kind of situation because, what if…

Russell Brand ’s wife, Laura Gallacher , is breaking her silence after the disgraced comedian was found guilty of rape and sexual assault and subsequently sentenced to more than 10 years in prison.

“[The show] may look different, but the ambitions are very much the same,” Gallacher, 39, said during the Sunday, November 15, episode of their YouTube series Sunday Service With the Brands . “And we trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything He’s doing right now, even though it’s painful.”

She continued, “And obviously, [it] will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me.”

Gallacher, however, shared she wants to continue with their series and feels “grateful for the support” and for viewers.

Russell Brand and Wife Laura Asked for Prayers in Podcast Before Sentencing 

“Although Russell is not here now in this moment, the holy spirit is moving and the holy spirit cannot be restrained,” she said. “I’m speaking to Russell. He’s OK and he’s praying, unsurprisingly. He’s praying and we decided for me to continue.”

Brand and Gallacher wed in 2017 and have since welcomed daughters Mabel and Peggy in 2016 and 2018, respectively, and a son in 2023.

items.title: Dove Cameron Details 'Special' Tribute to Late Cameron Boyce on New Song
items.summary:
Dove Cameron paid tribute to her late Descendants costar Cameron Boyce in her new song “Maybe Heaven Is a Jazz Club.”

“I think it became really special, too, when we put Cameron in the second verse ‘cause that wasn’t part of the plan,” Cameron, 30, recalled of the songwriting process on the Friday, November 13, episode of The Zach Sang Show . “ I didn’t have a second verse written, and when it got to that point, I had already started writing about, like, ‘Tired feet are never sore’ and all of these sort of dance things.”

Remembering how Boyce was an ”incredible dancer” during her lyrical session, the pop star soon realized the song would finally be complete with a recording of the late performer’s voice. (Boyce died in 2019 after suffering a seizure in his sleep. He was 20.)

“’Cause I met him at the jazz club / We’re playing for you from above / Yeah, I’ve seen him on the dance floor / Oh, he can’t get enough,” she sings in the chorus. “Tired feet are never sore / Crowd is begging him for more . Angel, you’re the one we’re waiting for / Baby, heaven is a jazz club.”

Late Cameron Boyce's Parents Still Love Hearing Stories of His Kindness 

The song ends with Boyce saying, “So, we’ll see you very soon.”

Before including Boyce’s voice in her song, Cameron reached out to his family for permission. (Cameron has remained close to Boyce’s parents, frequently attending his namesake foundation’s gala and inviting them to her wedding to Damiano David .)

items.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard Addresses Claims She Was Involved in Ken Urker's Death
items.summary:
Gypsy Rose Blanchard is admittedly still in disbelief that her former fiancé, Ken Urker , died.

“I just kept saying, ‘No, no, no, no, no, no, no. This isn’t true, you’re lying. You’re you’re making this up,’” Blanchard, 35, told 60 Minutes Australia in an interview broadcast on Sunday, November 15, recalling her initial reaction to Urker’s death. “I just hit the floor and I just remember screaming, screaming, screaming, screaming, ‘No, no, no.’”

Urker was found dead inside his Louisiana home last month on what was his 34th birthday. A cause of death has not been publicly revealed amid an ongoing investigation, while local police reports indicate the presence of drug paraphernalia on the scene. Another panellist, the TV presenter Dermot O’Leary, mimed picking up a phone and said: “When you’re dancing tonight, do you mind having sex afterwards?” Everyone laughed.

items.title: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood
items.summary:
After years of celebrity interviews, I have learned not to be fooled by the allure of fame. We never really know them – we know what they want us to know

As I sat in Southwark crown court, listening to the final day of Russell Brand’s trial, there was one subject that came up repeatedly, invoked as often by his defence as the prosecution. I don’t mean sex or coercion, but fame. It ran through every victim impact statement and loomed so large in the courtroom that it felt as if it was almost on trial itself.

I’m an entertainment journalist who has been covering celebrities for more than 20 years – as long as Brand has been one – and I have written about him at various stages of his career. But I went to Southwark crown court as a member of the public who wanted to see justice done. For the women he had hurt, for the ones who couldn’t get as far as the courtroom, and for all of us who came of age at a time when rape culture was so fast and furious that young women mistook it for a joke that we were in on. In the age of lads’ mags, sex felt cheapened, yet somehow we were the ones who ended up paying for this. So it was doubly strange to sit in court and feel somehow complicit in it - in how this media culture had encouraged Russell Brand.

Continue reading...
items.t: I saw how brightly stars like Russell Brand could shine, but there is darkness in the shadows | Sophie Heawood

items.title: Two courtrooms, one celebrity: how did the Russell Brand case compare with the rape trial next door?
items.summary:
One was a high-profile defendant watched by more than 100 journalists. Another was an unknown man who preyed on a girl almost half his age. Their stories played out minutes apart, one entirely out of the spotlight

What is going on inside Russell Brand’s head as he arrives at court for the start of his rape trial? He sees the dozens of cameras and journalists lined outside Southwark crown court, many of whom have been waiting since before 7am, and he tells himself that the media are all against him. “It seems to me that they believe that I am guilty, and that this should be the rubber-stamping of the process of my destruction.”

He walks with his wife, Laura, and his bodyguard past the photographers, “clickering, clackering, snickering paparazzi, like locusts, peculiar concoctions, not fully humans”, and up into the court, where he is suddenly overwhelmed by “the presence of something very beautiful, grace”. “In a situation like I’m in, it’s impossible not to turn to God. Truth and justice are the only things that can save me,” he thinks.
